OWN2-003.connection: Over F_q[T], with q a fixed prime power above an explicit threshold (q > 685.4 for twin primes, plus characteristic conditions) and the degree → ∞, they prove twin-prime/Chowla-type asymptotics via étale cohomology. ES has function-field variants (F26).

refs: Z.-W. Sun, Refining Lagrange's four-square theorem, J. Number Theory 175 (2017) 167–190

OWN2-012.title: Mihnea & Bogdan (arXiv 2509.00128, 2025): ES verified to 10¹⁸ with solution-count data f(p) — data for signature calibration
OWN2-012.connection: The paper extends verification to 10¹⁸ and evaluates the solution-counting function f(p) (F23, F04); check what count statistics are reported.

OWN2-014.connection: Davenport–Lewis–Schinzel: if f ∈ ℤ[t] and f(n) is a sum of two squares for every n, then f is a sum of two squares of polynomials; Cassels–Pfister: a polynomial that is a sum of k squares of rational functions is a sum of k squares of polynomials. These are the sums-of-squares analogues of 'no polynomial identity covers the square classes' (F09).

OWN2-016.connection: Trivial: x = y = z = p gives 1/p + 1/p + 2/p = 4/p. Also for p ≡ 1 (mod 4), x = (p+3)/4 leaves 12/(p(p+3)) = 3/N with N = p(p+3)/4, and 3/N = 1/N + 2/N. Breaking the unit-numerator symmetry kills the problem.

refs: J. Friedlander, H. Iwaniec, The polynomial X² + Y⁴ captures its primes, Ann. of Math. 148 (1998) 945–1040
D. R. Heath-Brown, Primes represented by x³ + 2y³, Acta Math. 186 (2001) 1–84

OWN2-019.connection: Each single ES line (e.g. (★) at a fixed level C) is expected to fail infinitely often (e.g. whenever 4Cp+1 is prime — infinitely often under Dickson/Schinzel); (★) overall fails at 14 primes ≤ 10¹⁰; ES itself is verified to 10¹⁸.

refs: R. L. Graham, On finite sums of reciprocals of distinct nth powers, Pacific J. Math. 14 (1964) 85–92
H. L. Montgomery, R. C. Vaughan, The exceptional set in Goldbach's problem, Acta Arith. 27 (1975) 353–370

OWN2-027.connection: ES witnesses have size ≤ poly(p) (F32). The distribution of the minimal possible max-denominator (or minimal level C) over hard primes is an observable comparable to 'least witness' problems (least nonresidue ≪ log² p under GRH, least prime in AP). Note (★) has no level at all for 14 primes ≤ 10¹⁰, so the level statistic needs the union with other lines.

OWN2-033.connection: Check whether in each GRH-success case (least nonresidue, Ramanujan's form x²+y²+10z², …) a single L-function or bounded family controls the event at the given n; caveat: Hooley's GRH proof of Artin uses infinitely many Kummer-field zeta functions and gives a density, so the criterion needs refinement. ES's event needs a family of size ≍ p of characters χ_{−4uB} at once.

OWN2-035.connection: Allowing one negative denominator turns the problem into an indefinite one; check whether the solution count then grows like n^δ (it stays finite unless 4/n is a unit fraction). The positive cone cuts it down to polylog.

refs: R. Hough, Solution of the minimum modulus problem for covering systems, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015) 361–382
Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, Tiba, On the Erdős covering problem: the density of the uncovered set, Invent. Math. 228 (2022)
Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, Tiba, The Erdős–Selfridge problem with square-free moduli, Algebra Number Theory 15 (2021)
OWN2-036.first_step: Check whether the BBMST criterion (stated for distinct moduli) applies to the list of ES identity classes (moduli ≤ 10⁵) and, if so, compute the guaranteed uncovered density.

OWN2-040.title: Graph-theoretic reformulation: bipartite 'divisor graph' between levels C and primes p; (★) ⟺ no isolated prime vertex
OWN2-040.connection: Make a bipartite graph with an edge (C, p) when R_C(p) > 0 ((★) divisor form at level C). (★)(p) ⟺ p has degree ≥ 1 — false at 14 primes ≤ 10¹⁰, so an ES version must add edges from other lines (e.g. the b = 1 line). Degree distribution ≍ Poisson(log²p) heuristically.

OWN2-042.why: So the set of p witnessed by (q, C) is one residue class mod q; (★)(p) for a hard prime p ⟸ p lies in some class {p ≡ −(4C)⁻¹ mod q : 4C | q+1} — an infinite covering by single residue classes (F34). These are (★) witnesses, so the covering misses the 14 (★)-failures ≤ 10¹⁰; for ES it must be combined with other lines. Note q ≥ 4C − 1, so q ≈ C scale.
